messages.name: addpoint
messages.description: Add a new point to the FluidDataSet. The dimensionality of the FluidDataSet is governed by the size of the first point added. If the identifier already exists, or if the size of the data does not match the dimensionality of the FluidDataSet an error will be reported. Argument details: identifier: buffer:

messages.name: print
messages.description: Post an abbreviated content of the DataSet in the window by default, but you can supply a custom action instead.

messages.name: read
messages.description: Replace the internal state of the object from a JSON file on disk. With no argument, a file dialog will appear to choose the file. It is always executed at the lowest priority on the main thread, usinginternally.

messages.name: refer
messages.description: Changes the reference to the data in another named fluid.dataset~ object. Changes to the data stored in any referenced will be shared by all other similarly named fluid.dataset~ objects.

messages.description: Callingwill change parameter values back to those the object waswith, i.e. any attribute values set in the box will be retained

messages.name: setpoint
messages.description: Set the point. If the identifier exists, this method behaves like updatePoint. If the identifier doesn't exist, it behaves like addPoint. Argument details: identifier: buffer:

messages.name: size
messages.description: The number of data points (entries / observations) in this model or dataset / labeset

messages.name: tobuffer
messages.description: Dump the content of the dataset to a, with optional transposition, and a map of frames/channels to the original IDs as a FluidLabelSet. Argument details: buffer: transpose: labelSet: labelwise:

messages.name: updatepoint
messages.description: Update an existing identifier's data. If the identifier does not exist, or if the size of the data does not match the dimensionality of the FluidDataSet an error will be reported. Argument details: identifier: buffer:

messages.name: write
messages.description: Save the internal state of the object to a JSON file on disk. With no argument, a file dialog will appear to choose the file. It is always executed at the lowest priority on the main thread, usinginternally.
